Subject: Gridline bake-off: performance benchmarking roadmap & MAP

Hi Sam —

Following up from last week’s call, I’ve attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a proposed performance bake-off roadmap. High level ask: we want to validate end-to-end latency and throughput characteristics across Redwood Hosted, a Dedicated pool, and a Private (VPC) deployment for your production-like workload so your SREs can pick the right tradeoffs for isolation and predictability.

Key objectives in the MAP:
- Measure median and P99 generation latency (TTFT and steady-state per-token) for representative prompts
- Validate throughput and concurrency saturation points (req/s and tokens/s) for 8k and 32k seq lengths
- Observe autoscaling behavior and cold-start/scale-down characteristics for Dedicated vs Private
- Confirm isolation: noise from noisy neighbors (mixed-tenant load) on Hosted vs Dedicated
- End-to-end reliability: tail latencies under bursty load, error rates, and fallback behavior

Request: can you share a small sample of production prompts (or an anonymized prompt suite) and a window for a 48-hour bake-off next week? We’ve included a test harness and checklist in the attachments: redwood-test-harness.tar.gz and sample-prompt-suite.jsonl.

Proposed close timeline in MAP:
- Week 1: MAP agreement + access enabling (credentials, dataset)
- Week 2: Bake-off runs and live dashboarding
- Week 3: Results review, recommendations, and PO/commit

I’ve looped in Marissa (Customer Success) for scheduling. Rishi will provide the technical test plan once we confirm dates.

Thanks —
Soojin

Subject: RE: Gridline bake-off: performance benchmarking roadmap & MAP

Sam / Soojin —

I’ve attached the technical test plan below; call-out summary here with explicit test cases and thresholds. Will run these across three deployment modes: Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Private (VPC-hosted instance). Tests will use your anonymized prompt suite and our harness.

Test matrix (summary):
- Scenarios: conversational streaming (low tokens per turn), long-context rerank (32k seq), batch recommendations (high tokens/s)
- Load shapes: steady (constant 120 concurrent sessions), spike (Poisson bursts to 350 concurrent), soak (48h continuous low variance)
- Metrics captured: TTFT (time-to-first-token), median and P99 per-request latency, tokens/sec throughput, GPU util, request error rate, autoscale latency (time to add/remove nodes), cold-start penalty (first request after scale), and cross-tenant noise (noise injection tests for Hosted)

Numeric pass/fail thresholds (examples):
- TTFT: median < 220ms (streaming), P99 < 850ms
- Per-request latency (32k rerank): median < 1.8s, P99 < 4.5s (Dedicated target)
- Throughput: sustain 3k tokens/s on Hosted for target model, Dedicated target 9k tokens/s (per pooled cluster), Private depends on cluster size but we’ll target equivalent to Dedicated in your VPC
- Concurrency: handle sustained 120 sessions with <1% error rate; handle spikes to 350 with graceful throttling/fallback under defined SLA
- Autoscaling behavior: Dedicated cluster should scale within 90s for additional nodes under our autoscaler; Private depends on your infra — we will instrument and measure

Test harness notes:
- We’ll run identical client drivers against each deployment (same seed and sequence distributions).
- For Hosted we’ll also run a noisy-neighbor pattern to validate isolation assumptions.
- We’ll capture raw traces and provide a result workbook with per-case breakdowns.

Deliverables:
- Live Grafana dashboard for the runs
- Result workbook with consolidated KPIs and recommended configuration (batching, quantization, routing policy)
- A short runbook highlighting operational caveats and suggested commit sizes for Dedicated/Private

Timeline:
- Tue (today): finalize test script and credentials
- Wed 00:00 PST: start 48h run
- Fri 10:00 PST: results review (30–45m) + recommendation memo by EOD Friday

If you want, we can carve a short canary subset to run on Wed evening first (4 hours) to validate harness and credentials before the full 48h.

— Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
